title: Worst to First: Sonny's Ben Dover Climbs Out of the Basement and Wins Buckaroo Bowl III
dek: After two straight last-place finishes, the commissioner went 13-3 and beat Randy's The fumblers for the title, while Mekhi's Dawgs scored the second-most points in the league and still ended up at the bottom.
body: For two years, Ben Dover was the league's cautionary tale, finishing last in 2023 and again in 2024. In 2025, Sonny flipped the script so hard it almost tore. Ben Dover went 13-3, took the No. 1 seed, and won Buckaroo Bowl III, ending Kaushal's two-year reign and putting a brand-new name on the trophy. The guy who built the league website finally has something worth putting on the homepage.

The regular season belonged to the commish, and the rest of the standings were a mess. Ben Dover's 13-3 mark was four games better than anyone else, and its 1850.8 points were enough even though three teams were within shouting distance. Randy's The fumblers grabbed the 2 seed at 9-7, Kaushal's Habibsters took the 3 seed at 8-8, and Mekhi's Dawgs claimed the 4 seed at 8-8. Ramon's Remains and Alan's Team Pillbert, both 5-11, filled out the bottom two seeds. The commissioner will insist none of this was an abuse of power, and for once the record backs him up.

Kaushal deserves a moment of sympathy. Habibsters led the league with 1973.6 points, more than 120 ahead of the champion, and still finished exactly .500. Then came the playoffs, where Randy's team dropped 137.1 on Habib and held Habibsters to 79.96, a 57-point beatdown that ended the two-time champ's bid for a three-peat. It was the best afternoon of Randy's postseason and the worst possible week for the league's top offense to go quiet, and it sent the defending dynasty home with a third-place finish.

That put The fumblers in Buckaroo Bowl III against Ben Dover, and the final belonged to Sonny. Ben Dover won 105.1 to 86.48, a 19-point margin that was comfortable without being a cakewalk. Randy got further than he ever had in this league, which should give him plenty to grumble about all offseason, but the trophy went to the manager who spent two years climbing the consolation ladder in the wrong direction. Somewhere in Boston, a newly minted champion is presumably learning to pronounce "wicked good" without irony.

The strangest story of the year happened at the bottom. Mekhi's Dawgs scored 1858.2 points, the second-most in the league and more than the champion, and posted the season's best single week with 153.62 in Week 9. Kai also made the playoffs as the 4 seed. And yet, when the consolation ladder finished sorting things out, Dawgs landed in sixth, while Alan's 5-11 Team Pillbert, the bracket's lowest seed, climbed all the way to fourth. Leave it to Philly to lose 11 games and still finish ahead of the second-best offense in the league.

Then there's the asterisk. Ramon ran Araleasers through Week 8, including the season's lowest score, a 61.4 in Week 3, before getting kicked from the league for inactivity. The team was renamed Ramon's Remains and played out the year without him, and its first game as an orphan was a 94.76 to 92.02 win over Alan in Week 9. The Remains finished 5-11 with a league-low 1523.7 points and took fifth, and every one of those post-Week 8 results stays on Brucie's record, asterisk and all.

One last first for the record books: four trades. After two seasons in which nobody made a single deal, the 2025 market finally opened for business. It was a season of firsts all around, with a first-time champion, a first-time finalist in Randy, and a first-time trip to the cellar for Mekhi's points machine. The league expands to eight teams in 2026, and for the first time, everyone is chasing Sonny.
